newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - July 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - July 8.

text.p: Following are the highlights of Irish press on Tuesday:
- A leaked document dealt a lethal blow to Northern Secretary Mo Mowlam's peace strategy last night as rioting continued and a policeman was shot.
- Retired paediatrician Victoria Coffey said she had presented babies for a drug trial at a Dublin children's home more than 30 years ago.
- Dunnes Stores are to press for the recovery of 1.3 million they contend was paid by Ben Dunne to former prime minister Charles Haughey.

- A confidential document leaked in Belfast last night indicates the Northern Ireland Office had decided that the best policy was to let the Drumcree march go down the Garvaghy Road if there was no agreement between the opposing factions.
- A policeman was shot on the Garvaghy Road early this morning as rioting and violence continued throughout Northern Ireland.
- Thirteen new ministers of state are expected to be approved by the cabinet today.
- The pound's fall to 90 pence sterling threatens to cause problems for the government and the central bank in the weeks ahead.
- A loyalist bomb maker was killed and Sinn Fein MP Martin McGuinness was injured as another night of mayhem gripped the North and left the peace process in tatters.

- Northern nationalists were incensed last night when a Northern Ireland Office document, leaked by a Catholic civil servant to journalists in Belfast, revealed that only one option was ever considered in the run-up to the crisis, a march of some kind through the nationalist Garvaghy Road.
- Legal hurdles have been cleared to allow vital evidence from Ben Dunne's solicitor Noel Smyth to be heard at the Dunnes Stores Tribunal later today.
